newsitem.title: VATICAN: Pope says chemical weapons ban must be real.
newsitem.headline: Pope says chemical weapons ban must be real.

text.p: Pope John Paul on Wednesday welcomed the entry into force of a treaty banning chemical weapons but said government leaders had to ensure that its provisions rapidly become reality.
Addressing pilgrims in St Peter's Square after his weekly general audience, the leader of the world's Roman Catholics said chemical weapons were an "immense danger for the whole world".
He welcomed the new treaty, which came into force at the end of April and bans the development, production, stockpiling and use of chemical weapons, but added:

"I appeal to government leaders to work without delay to put into practice what the relevant convention foresees. All of humanity expects such an attitude so that it can look to the future with greater serenity."
The treaty has been hailed as the most ambitious disarmament agreement ever because it seeks to eliminate an entire class of weapons and includes unprecedented verification measures.
The United States Senate ratified the treaty just five days before it entered force on April 29.
A total of 88 countries have ratified the treaty and a further 77 countries, including Russia, have signed it but not yet ratified it.
Russia and the United States are the two biggest holders of chemical weapons, with combined stocks of 70,000 tonnes.
Under the treaty, member states must destroy their chemical weapons within 10 years and provide detailed information about the production and export of listed chemicals used to make such weapons.
Countries which remain outside the treaty include Iraq, Libya, North Korea and Syria.
